title: Relocating a Washer/Dryer to a First-Floor Bathroom Closet (Ask This Old House)

locations.name: First-floor bathroom closet (proposed washer/dryer location)
locations.basis: Transcript describes converting bathroom closet into laundry space and placing washer/dryer there

locations.name: Basement/cellar laundry area (original location)
locations.basis: Transcript notes the laundry was previously downstairs in the cellar/basement

summary: This This Old House episode documents a couple’s plan to relocate their laundry from a basement/ cellar to a first-floor bathroom closet to support aging in place and eliminate stairs. The project team evaluates the closet size, plumbing, and vent routing; discusses electrical service upgrades (upgrading to 200A with dedicated circuits for a washer and a dryer); coordinates a trades team (electrician and carpenter); plans framing, door repositioning, and finish carpentry to create a neat, accessible laundry niche. The workflow covers wiring runs through the ceiling, completing a rough-in for new 20A/120V and 30A/240V circuits, venting, water shutoffs, a valve box, and a planning path that keeps existing appliances functional during the remodel. The episode also highlights practical considerations for aging-in-place design, including door clearances, thresholds, and accessible controls, culminating in a demonstration of the new stacked washer-dryer installation.

sections.title: Intro and home goals
sections.description: Jim and Michelle discuss aging in place and wanting to eliminate stairs by moving laundry to the first floor. They outline the bathroom renovation so accessibility features can be included and set the objective to relocate the washer/dryer from the basement to a closet near the hallway.

sections.title: Closet feasibility for laundry
sections.description: The team evaluates the bathroom closet as the potential washer/dryer site, noting available drain, hot/cold piping, and the vent path. They acknowledge the closet’s proximity to bathroom plumbing and the adjacency to the hallway.

sections.title: Team setup and scope
concepts: Deciding between basement versus upstairs services
sections.description: Richard calls in Heath (electrician) and Nathan (carpenter) to join the project. They discuss whether to relocate the washer/dryer upstairs or keep the existing basement setup and start outlining the electrical and plumbing scope.

sections.title: Electrical planning and service needs
sections.description: The team confirms the need for a new 200A service and a larger panel, while planning to duplicate the existing circuits: a 20A, 120V circuit for the washer upstairs and a 30A circuit for the dryer. They also discuss relocating a thermostat and preparing for future mechanical elements.

sections.title: Wiring, venting, and rough-in
concepts: Turning off main power for safety
sections.description: The crew runs the electrical cabling (12-2 for washer, 10-3 for dryer) after locking out the main breaker. They frame the rough opening for the new closet doorway, set thresholds, and plan a neat path for wiring alongside building services. A telescoping dryer vent and vent placement above the shower area are reviewed to ensure proper clearance and fit.

sections.title: Door and wall finish planning
sections.description: Attention turns to making the space feel integrated: adjusting door swing, using cedar shims for plumb, and installing flush thresholds so the washer/dryer can roll in easily. They discuss finish details like maple trim and a paneled wall look to blend with the house.

sections.title: Wrap-up and homeowner reflection
sections.description: The team wraps up with a final demonstration of the new stacked washer/dryer configuration and thanks the homeowners. They invite viewers to submit ideas for other projects and sign off with credits and call-to-action to subscribe.
